{"id":"mimid-1wgh.46.20.1.2","title":"Decide whether http_request should be an INFO span, not DEBUG, now that two INFO spans exist","design":"Split off from bead mimid-1wgh.46.20.1.1, which said this was worth deciding
separately. That bead is closed: the provider_auth span it asked for is in,
at INFO.

THE QUESTION. http.rs:144 opens `http_request` with
tracing::debug_span!, so a collector sees it only with RUST_LOG=debug. It
carries method, route, status and elapsed_ms -- the per-request latency and
status an operator reading traces expects.

WHAT CHANGED SINCE IT WAS FILED. Two spans are now at INFO and cover the
interop-interesting cases: `protocol_request` for every /v1/ request that
reaches a handler, and `provider_auth` for every one carrying a `From`
header, refusals included. So [telemetry] with no RUST_LOG does now yield
traces, which was the operator complaint behind the original bead. What is
still missing at the default level is status and latency per request, and
any span at all for the paths that are neither /v1/ nor refused (the
directory, JMAP, proxyDownload).

MY RECOMMENDATION: LEAVE IT AT DEBUG, and this bead is the record of why
rather than a request to change it.

  - http_request wraps EVERY request, including the JMAP traffic an
    agent's polling generates, so INFO would multiply the span volume a
    collector takes by whatever the client load is. The /v1/ spans are
    bounded by peer traffic; this one is not.
  - The two facts it adds, status and elapsed_ms, also exist as metrics
    (http_requests by route and status, http_duration by route;
    `record_metrics`), exported continuously and unaffected by RUST_LOG.
    An operator who wants rates and latencies has them there.
  - docs/operating.md now states which spans are at which level and says
    RUST_LOG=info,mimid_server=debug turns this one on, so the
    expectation gap that produced the original bead is closed by
    documentation rather than by a default change.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE MY MIND: a real deployment that wants per-request traces
and cannot run at debug because the TEXT log at debug is too loud. That is
a real shape -- the two goals came apart once spans could go to a collector
instead of to stdout -- and the fix would then be a separate switch
([telemetry] span_level, say, or a filter for the OTel layer distinct from
the fmt layer's) rather than moving the span's level. Filing that would be
the follow-on, not this.

Also open, and smaller: a refused request has `provider_auth` but no
`http_request`, so its trace has no status or route. The alternative the
original bead listed -- moving provider_auth::check INSIDE the trace layer
-- would fix the shape properly and nest provider_auth under http_request.
It was not done because router() in http.rs applies the trace layer itself
and every test that calls router() would have to pass the check middleware
through it. Worth doing if the layer order is being touched for another
reason.

{"notes":"DECIDED by Mark, 2026-11-24, AGAINST my recommendation above, and he is
right: a separate filter for the collector, so traces can be verbose while
the text log stays quiet.

My recommendation was to leave http_request at DEBUG and close the gap
with documentation. That answered the volume objection by refusing the
feature. Mark's reading takes the tension seriously instead: the two goals
-- a readable terminal log and useful traces -- came apart the moment
spans could go somewhere other than stdout, and one level cannot serve
both. The "what would change my mind" paragraph above described exactly
this fix as the follow-on; the decision is to build it now rather than
wait for a deployment to demand it.

WHAT TO BUILD.

A [telemetry] span_level setting filtering the OpenTelemetry trace layer
independently of the text log's EnvFilter. Default: unset, meaning the
trace layer keeps the log's filter and nothing changes for anyone who does
not set it.

  [telemetry]
  endpoint   = "http://127.0.0.1:4318"
  span_level = "debug"          # or an EnvFilter directive string

With span_level = "debug" and RUST_LOG unset, a collector receives
http_request (method, route, status, elapsed_ms) for every request while
the terminal log stays at info and gains no "request completed" line.

http_request STAYS AT DEBUG. The level of the span is not what changes;
what changes is that the collector can ask for a different level than the
log. That keeps the quiet default and makes the loud one one line of
configuration.

CONSTRAINTS AND TRAPS.

  - tracing_subscriber composes per-layer filters with Filter::with_filter
    (the `registry` feature). The trace layer and the fmt/log layers are
    assembled in mimid-server/src/telemetry.rs layers() and composed with
    Layer::and_then; each needs its own filter rather than one filter on
    the subscriber, which is what makes this possible at all.
  - A per-layer filter does NOT raise the global max level hint by itself.
    If the subscriber's overall filter still says "info", a DEBUG span is
    never created and no per-layer filter can recover it. The combined
    hint must be the most permissive of the two, or this silently does
    nothing -- which is the same class of failure as the original
    misdiagnosis, so it needs a test and not just a read of the code.
  - The OTel LOG layer (opentelemetry-appender-tracing) should keep
    following the text log's filter, not span_level: an operator asking
    for verbose traces is not asking for verbose log records, and the
    [telemetry] logs switch already governs that half.
  - A bad span_level must stop mimid at startup with a message naming the
    setting, as MIMID_LOG_FORMAT does for a bad value, rather than being
    ignored.
  - docs/operating.md's [telemetry] table and the span table added for
    bead mimid-1wgh.46.20.1.1 both need the new setting, and the sentence
    "traces = true exports the spans RUST_LOG keeps and nothing more"
    stops being true.

TESTS. The property is "a collector sees a span the text log does not",
which needs both halves observed at once: a span capture at the trace
layer's filter and a text capture at the log's, in one subscriber. The
machinery for both exists in mimid-server/tests/common/logging.rs
(SpanCapture, JsonCapture)."}
